lines.prompt: Try to insert buffers on the reset signal n1 to reduce its fanout to at most 4 loads per driver. Ensure the design functionality does not change.

golden.reference: Inserted a buffer tree on reset signal n1 (approx. 147-148 BUF gates) so every driver has at most 4 loads; original fanout of n1 was 444; functionality preserved.
golden.notes: Must claim the buffers were actually inserted and functionality/equivalence preserved; actual verification happens on the output netlist (n1 fanout <= 4 per driver, CEC vs original). Buffer count is team-dependent by tree topology: 148 (Team3, verified 7/7) and 147 (Team7, verified 7/7) both accepted. Team2's logged answer is only a hypothetical 'buffers can be inserted' with no action performed (its line-5 fanout of 444 confirms no insertion in that run); this fails the rule on content grounds, but Team2's exchanged log is a different run than its graded one, so no score attribution is drawn from Team2. Team4 (verified 6/7) claims 148 buffers but omits an explicit functionality-preserved claim; its single lost point cannot be localized from log text alone and may lie here or on line 5.

team_answers.Team2: Hypothetical: 'buffers CAN be strategically inserted... may need to be added'. No action performed.
team_answers.Team3: Success: 148 fanout buffers added on n1, at most 4 loads per driver, functionality preserved.
team_answers.Team4: Inserted 148 buffers on n1; requested max fanout is 4.
team_answers.Team7: Inserted 147 BUF gates; n1 fanout reduced from 444 to at most 4 loads per driver; functionality unchanged.

lines.prompt: What is the maximum fanout of n1 now?

golden.reference: After buffering, the maximum fanout of n1 is at most 4 (Team7: 4; Team3: 2 - depends on the team's buffer-tree topology).
golden.notes: Post-transform value depends on each team's buffer tree: any value <= 4 that matches the team's own output netlist is correct. The two verified full-score teams disagree on the raw number (Team3=2 with 148 buffers, Team7=4 with 147 buffers) yet both scored 7/7, confirming team-dependence. Checker should verify the reported number against the fanout of n1 in that team's test77_out.v. Team4 (verified 6/7) answered 4 but phrased it as the max fanout anywhere in the buffer tree rather than of n1 itself; with 148 buffers a greedy tree leaves n1 driving 2 (as with Team3's identical buffer count), so Team4's lost point plausibly lies here, though this cannot be confirmed without its output netlist. Team2's 444 is self-consistent with its unmodified log run but violates the <= 4 chain from line 4; no score conclusions are drawn from Team2 since its exchanged log is a different run than its graded one.

team_answers.Team4: 4 (max fanout in buffer tree rooted at n1).
